Information since May points to a strong labor market and solid economic activity, with headline and core inflation near the symmetric 2 percent objective and longer-term expectations little changed. In the inflation-targeting literature, anchoring expectations near target (Svensson; Woodford) supports credibility and mitigates the classic inflation bias highlighted by Barro-Gordon, keeping welfare costs of inflation moderate. The decision to raise the federal funds rate and signal further gradual increases aligns with Taylor-rule style responses to tight labor markets and inflation near target, consistent with New Keynesian Phillips-curve stabilization. Implementation via IOER and the RRP to keep the effective rate within range, alongside steady balance-sheet runoff, is designed to normalize policy without abrupt credit tightening, mindful of financial-friction channels. Overall tone is positive but hawkish-leaning: strong current conditions with prudent, credibility-preserving normalization.
